rule: trajectory-level split; every sample of a trajectory belongs to exactly one partition; test and validation trajectories are never used for training or for hyper-parameter selection

allowed_inputs: snap status from the Phase 3a.1 trajectory audit
selection_basis.authored_by: Phase 3a.1, from the Task A audit only

test_design.t04_sprint_corner: sprinting - mean speed 18.2 m/s, peak 84.1 m/s
test_design.t06_look_around: pure rotation - stationary (mean speed 0.0 m/s) with the highest sustained rotation of any trajectory (mean 26.8 deg/s)
test_design.t01_walk_straight: translation-dominant - constant 6 m/s, zero rotation over the whole trajectory
test_design.t03_walk_corner: walking - 6 m/s with a single corner (mean rotation 4.1 deg/s)

validation_design.t05_turn_left_right: rotation-heavy while moving (mean rotation 14.9 deg/s, mean speed 4.6 m/s)
validation_design.t07_stop_start: stop/start translation with almost no rotation (mean rotation 0.9 deg/s)
validation_design.t08_forward_reverse: translation including reverse (mean speed 5.4 m/s, mean rotation 1.0 deg/s)

training_design.rationale: retains one trajectory of every movement type that has more than one member, so no replicated behaviour is missing from training
training_design.singleton_absent_reason: four movement types are represented by exactly one trajectory each; because the test and validation sets must hold out seven trajectories and only three types have a second member, at least four singleton types cannot appear in training. See docs/experimental-split-review.md for the trade-off.

snap_policy.reason: the three yaw snaps are generator defects (Phase 3a.1 Task A.3), so keeping those trajectories out of test and validation prevents scoring on artefacts
snap_policy.row_level_policy: snap-affected rows are additionally excluded from headline metrics everywhere and reported separately; the same exclusion is recommended for training data in Phase 3b
